blogs.name: Simon Willison
blogs.title: Muru
blogs.description: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 2026-11-05 — A first look at Muru 2026-11-07 — Muru: looking inside the workers 2026-11-08 — Muru: how it fits together 2026-11-09 — Muru: import once, fork many 2026-11-10 — Muru: HTTPS in development 2026-11-11 — Muru: WSGI and ASGI together 2026-11-11 — AI as a lifestyle choice 2026-11-12 — Muru: releases, not restarts 2026-11-13 — Muru: canaries without a service mesh 2026-11-14 — Muru: a better tenant in a container 2026-11-15 — Muru: working with Kubernetes, not around it 2026-11-16 — Muru: scaling from what the workers report 2026-11-17 — Muru: scaling to zero 2026-11-18 — Muru: overlays on a schedule 2026-11-19 — Muru: noticing and responding 2026-11-20 — Muru: a toolbar on every page 2026-11-21 — Muru: tracing in the toolbar 2026-11-22 — Muru: when lazy imports help That post about AI as a lifestyle choice is particularly worth a read: The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too. Tags: graham-dumpleton , modwsgi , python , wsgi , ai , rust , asgi , generative-ai , llms , ai-assisted-programming

blogs.name: Simon Willison
blogs.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
blogs.description: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. — Ravi Vakil , Hurried Announcement: Alessandro Masullo GRH Tags: mathematics

blogs.title: Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model
blogs.description: Z.ai is moving its flagship GLM-5.4 model to a loop architecture in which 28 layers run twice, which the company says lets the 750-billion-parameter model match models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters. Benchmark scores are only available for a smaller 30B test model so far, and Z.ai is positioning GLM-5.4 as the start of "Generalized Coding," where code also generates videos, games, and CAD models. The article Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model appeared first on The Decoder .
